outcome_detail: No resolution reported as of mid-2026; 2024 and 2026 coverage continues to describe the RNC civil cases (four suits, ten women) as active litigation against the provincial government.
criminal_detail: May 2024 reporting states no criminal charges have been laid in relation to the allegations in these suits; the plaintiffs' lawyer said the women pursued civil suits because they had lost confidence in the criminal courts. NL's Serious Incident Response Team was reported in 2021 to be investigating sexual-offence allegations against several RNC officers; no resulting charges tied to this suit have been reported.
incident_date_approx: 2001-2017, mostly downtown St. John's (George Street area)
description: Seven women filed a joint statement of claim on Sept. 9, 2022 in the Supreme Court of Newfoundland and Labrador, alleging they were sexually assaulted between 2001 and 2017 by various on-duty Royal Newfoundland Constabulary officers who offered them rides home at night, mostly from the bar-lined George Street area of downtown St. John's. The suit names the Government of Newfoundland and Labrador, which is responsible for the force, as the sole defendant, and alleges the government knew or ought to have known that officers were targeting women in the St. John's area and failed in its duty to warn the public. Retired Sgt. Robert Baldwin is the only officer identified by name in the suit; he denies all allegations against him. The allegations have not been tested in court, and no criminal charges have been laid.
notes: Single statement of claim with seven plaintiffs against one defendant (the province) — kept as one record. Companion records from the same scandal: rec-78 (RNC officer's suit, Jan. 2022), rec-80 and rec-80b (two suits filed March 2024).
